cues.en: Instructor: In this video, I want to introduce you to a concept in correlation analysis that here in the title I'm calling the subgroups correlation paradox.
cues.zh: 講師：這支影片要介紹相關分析的一個概念，標題中我稱為子群相關悖論。

cues.en: The official term for this is Simpson's Paradox, but I didn't wanna use Simpson's Paradox in the title of the video because I was afraid you might think that this was
cues.zh: 正式名稱是辛普森悖論，但我不想在影片標題使用這個名字，因為怕你以為這是在講

cues.en: about a Simpson's Halloween special or something.
cues.zh: 《辛普森家庭》的萬聖節特別篇之類的。

cues.en: So anyway, here we have a dataset.
cues.zh: 總之，這裡有一份資料集。

cues.en: Now, ignore for the moment the color, just look at the distribution of all the dots in this plot.
cues.zh: 先忽略顏色，只看圖中所有點的分布。

cues.en: You can see visually it's super clear that there is a strong linear relationship between variable X and variable Y.
cues.zh: 視覺上非常清楚，X 與 Y 有很強的線性關係。

cues.en: And in fact, the correlation between X and Y across this population of dots is almost 0.8.
cues.zh: 事實上，這整群點的 X 與 Y 相關，幾乎是 0.8。

cues.en: And the P value is tiny.
cues.zh: 而且 P 值極小。

cues.en: It's really, really small.
cues.zh: 真的非常非常小。

cues.en: So this is definitely a statistically significant positive correlation between these two variables.
cues.zh: 因此，這肯定是兩個變數之間統計顯著的正相關。

cues.en: However, notice what happens when I compute the correlation within each of these subgroups separately.
cues.zh: 但注意，分別計算各個子群的相關，會發生什麼事。

cues.en: So this is the correlation coefficient and the p-value only for the red dots.
cues.zh: 這是只針對紅點計算的相關係數與 P 值。

cues.en: So ignoring the blue dots and the black dots.
cues.zh: 忽略藍點與黑點。

cues.en: And here the correlation is 0.2, non-significant.
cues.zh: 這裡相關是 0.2，不顯著。

cues.en: The p-value is 0.4.
cues.zh: P 值是 0.4。

cues.en: For the blue dots here, if anything, it's a negative correlation, minus 0.3.
cues.zh: 藍點如果有什麼相關，反而是負相關，負 0.3。

cues.en: Now, it's not significant.
cues.zh: 不過它不顯著。

cues.en: So we can't really interpret this value, but numerically it's a negative relationship.
cues.zh: 因此不能真正解讀這個值，但數值上是負向關係。

cues.en: And yeah, the black dots are correlated at basically zero.
cues.zh: 黑點的相關基本上是 0。

cues.en: Also very non-significant.
cues.zh: 同樣非常不顯著。

cues.en: So we have three groups that individually correlate non-significantly, which means that correlation coefficient is not distinguishable from zero.
cues.zh: 所以，三組各自的相關都不顯著，也就是相關係數無法與 0 區分。

cues.en: And then we put them all together and we get a really robust correlation, really strong relationship, highly, highly significant.
cues.zh: 但把它們合在一起，就得到很穩健的相關、很強的關係，而且高度顯著。

cues.en: So what is going on here?
cues.zh: 這是怎麼回事？

cues.en: What is reality?
cues.zh: 真相究竟是什麼？

cues.en: Well, this is the Simpson's paradox.
cues.zh: 這就是辛普森悖論。

cues.en: In fact, it can get even weirder than this because you can show a similar effect where each individual group has a negative correlation, a significant negative correlation.
cues.zh: 實際上還可以更奇怪：每個個別群組都具有負相關，而且是顯著負相關，也能出現類似效果。

cues.en: And in fact, if you look up Simpson's Paradox on the internet, you can also come across pictures where they show a negative correlation within each subgroup,
cues.zh: 如果上網查辛普森悖論，也會看到圖示，每個子群內都是負相關，

cues.en: and then a positive correlation overall.
cues.zh: 整體卻呈現正相關。

cues.en: So what is the right thing to do here?
cues.zh: 那應該怎麼做才對？

cues.en: Well, in this case, these are simulated data.
cues.zh: 這個例子是模擬資料。

cues.en: I just made up these numbers.
cues.zh: 數字都是我編的。

cues.en: So it's hard to argue what is the correct interpretation in this dataset.
cues.zh: 所以很難爭論，這份資料集哪種解讀才正確。

cues.en: If you encounter something like this in your dataset, then essentially what you have to do is make a determination, make a decision about whether these subgroups are
cues.zh: 如果你的資料集出現這種情況，基本上必須判斷、決定這些子群之間，

cues.en: qualitatively distinct from each other.
cues.zh: 是否存在本質上的差異。

cues.en: If they're really different from each other, maybe they come from totally different samples, different populations, they have some other underlying difference.
cues.zh: 如果它們真的不同，可能來自完全不同的樣本、不同母體，或有其他底層差異。

cues.en: If they're really qualitatively different, categorically different from each other, then it's more appropriate to interpret these correlations, rather than pulling them together.
cues.zh: 如果本質上、類別上確實不同，解讀這些個別相關，就比合併在一起更適合。

cues.en: On the other hand, if these different subgroups are all closely related and you don't have any meaningful scientific justification
cues.zh: 另一方面，如果這些子群都密切相關，而且沒有有意義的科學理由，

cues.en: for splitting them up into groups, then this is actually not the appropriate way to subgroup.
cues.zh: 支持把它們分成不同群組，那這種分組方式其實就不合適。

cues.en: And instead, you would interpret this correlation.
cues.zh: 反而應該解讀這個整體相關。

cues.en: So you can see that whether you interpret the total correlation or the individual subgroups' correlations is not something that I can just tell you which way to go.
cues.zh: 所以，要解讀整體相關，還是各個子群的相關，並不是我能直接告訴你該選哪一種。

cues.en: It's something you have to make a determination about based on your data, based on your experiment and so on.
cues.zh: 必須根據你的資料、實驗等等，自行判斷。

cues.en: So in this video, I just wanted to point this out to you and make sure that you are aware of this phenomenon called Simpson's Paradox and how to make a decision about which of these,
cues.zh: 這支影片只是想指出這個現象，確保你知道辛普森悖論，以及如何決定這些相關之中，

cues.en: whether it's appropriate to interpret correlations of subgroups.
cues.zh: 是否適合解讀子群的相關。

cues.en: Now, there's a code here, I'm showing the MATLAB code.
cues.zh: 這裡有程式碼，展示的是 MATLAB 程式碼。

cues.en: Of course, there's also corresponding Python code.
cues.zh: 當然，也有對應的 Python 程式碼。

cues.en: I'm not gonna go through it line by line because there isn't really anything terribly new in the code that you haven't already learned in previous videos in this course.
cues.zh: 不會逐行說明，因為裡面沒有太多本課程先前影片尚未學過的新內容。

cues.en: So the code is here for your edification.
cues.zh: 程式碼放在這裡，供你學習。

cues.en: If you're curious, you can go through it.
cues.zh: 有興趣可以自行研究。

cues.en: If you would like to give yourself a little bit of a challenge, a little bit of a code challenge, you can try changing, modifying the code, the MATLAB code or the Python code
cues.zh: 如果想給自己一點程式挑戰，可以試著改寫 MATLAB 或 Python 程式碼，

cues.en: to implement what I mentioned before where you can actually have negative correlations of the subgroups, so statistically significantly negative correlations, and then still a positive overall correlation.
cues.zh: 實作剛才提到的情況：各個子群呈現統計顯著的負相關，整體卻仍然是正相關。

cues.en: So that could be something you could do if you're curious.
cues.zh: 有興趣的話，可以試試看。
